https://www.flickeringmyth.com/the-movie.text: Matthew Shepherd revisits Susanne Bier’s Serena starring Bradley Cooper and Jennifer Lawrence… Bradley Cooper rarely talks about Serena . Jennifer Lawrence does not either. This felt odd until learning more about it, now it makes a lore more sense. In early 2012, the two of them filmed a Depression-era period drama in the Czech Republic directed by Oscar-winning Danish filmmaker Susanne Bier, based on a critically acclaimed novel by Ron Rash, for a budget of $25 to $30 million. It was, on paper, exactly the kind of serious prestige film that serious actors make between franchise obligations to remind the industry they have range. Then Silver Linings Playbook came out. Then The Hunger Games sequel. Then American Hustle . By the time Serena finally reached audiences, Cooper and Lawrence had become two of the most bankable stars on the planet — and the film they had made together before any of that happened had been sitting in an editing suite for two years, quietly becoming one of the great film mysteries of that decade. The premise is straightforward period drama. George Pemberton, played by Cooper, is an ambitious timber baron operating in the mountains of Depression-era North Carolina. He falls for and marries Serena Shaw, played by Lawrence — a fiercely independent woman with a tragic past who immediately proves herself the sharper business mind of the two. When Serena discovers she cannot have children, the marriage begins to fracture under the weight of her obsession with the business and George’s growing entanglement with a former lover who has borne him a son. It is a dark, literary story about power, ambition, and the specific violence of a marriage built on mutual ruthlessness. The source novel was well-regarded. The director had an Academy Award. The cast had chemistry that Silver Linings Playbook had already proven to audiences worldwide. There was one thing nobody had anticipated though, and that was Silver Linings Playbook . Serena was filmed in early 2012, before either Cooper or Lawrence had broken into the first tier of Hollywood. Cooper was recognisable from The Hangover ; Lawrence was known for Winter’s Bone and the first Hunger Games . Neither was yet the phenomenon they would become. By the time Bier had finished a first cut, Silver Linings Playbook had been released, Lawrence had won an Academy Award for it at twenty-two, and the film landscape around Serena had shifted entirely. The project that had been greenlit as a modest prestige drama was now carrying the weight of two of the industry’s most scrutinised careers. Bier had a reputation in film circles as a perfectionist, and the post-production process reflected it. She went through multiple cuts over an eighteen-month editing period, reportedly paralysed by the difficulty of arriving at a version she was satisfied with. Insiders maintained the delay was purely about Bier’s perfectionism rather than any fundamental problem with the footage, though there was also a growing sense that the film could not possibly live up to what Silver Linings Playbook had made audiences expect from a Cooper and Lawrence pairing. CAA screened the finished film for studio buyers and several made offers, but none were substantial enough to justify a wide release. No American distributor bit. The film was eventually acquired by Magnolia Pictures for the United States and StudioCanal for the UK and Europe — modest specialty distributors rather than the studio machinery a film of this profile might reasonably have expected. It premiered at the BFI London Film Festival in October 2014, more than two years after filming had wrapped. At the premiere there was an almost eerie sense that both Lawrence and Cooper were contractually obligated to attend — that they had already moved on entirely and were returning to something they had left behind long ago. The numbers that followed were among the most brutal in recent prestige film history. In the UK, the film opened across 185 theatres to just £153,000, averaging £827 per screen, and closed its entire run with under £321,000. The American release was arguably worse. Serena opened in 59 theatres to $100,090, lost 27 of those theatres in its second weekend, declined 76% and closed with $176,391 in total. In a final indignity, it was made available on iTunes and Google Play for rental three weeks before it reached American theatres — an effective admission that the theatrical release was a formality rather than a genuine commercial play. The critical reception did nothing to complicate this picture. Reviews described Lawrence as miscast — too young and luminous for a role that required weathered severity — and the script as too scattered to honour what made the novel work. The consensus was not that Serena was a disaster in the Collateral Beauty mould, a film that had actively deceived its audience. It was something quieter and more deflating: a competent, handsome film that had simply been overtaken by events outside anyone’s control. What makes Serena this series’ most melancholy entry is that nobody made a catastrophic decision. Bier was not wrong to take her time. Cooper and Lawrence were not wrong to move on to the projects that made them stars. The distributors who passed were not wrong to calculate that the audience for this film had evaporated. The tragedy, if it can be called that, is purely one of timing. A film shot six months later, or released six months earlier, might have found the window it needed. Instead it arrived two years too late, carrying the weight of careers it had helped create without receiving any of the credit. Can you remember Serena ? Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Aldi saw the smallest increase in a basket of common items such as apples, mince and rice. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images Consumer affairs Groceries rise by 7% across Australian supermarket chains, Choice finds The price of a basket of items in Coles, Woolworths, IGA and Aldi increased to an average of $43.62, survey says Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter Wed 23 Sep 2026 11.01 EDT Last modified on Wed 23 Sep 2026 11.03 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Groceries have become more expensive at all four of Australia’s major supermarket chains, with the average price of a basket of essentials increasing by 7% between March and June, new analysis has found. The consumer advocacy group Choice on Thursday released its 10th quarterly government-funded survey of supermarket prices, which it assessed by filling a basket with eight common grocery items at 104 different stores in June. The basket – containing milk, royal gala apples, strawberries, bananas, potatoes, avocado, basmati rice and beef mince – increased in price by 7% across Coles, Woolworths , Aldi, and IGA since Choice’s last survey in March. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here The total cost of the eight items – averaged across all the stores – went up by $2.79 between March and June, from $40.83 to $43.62. Choice released its latest grocery price survey as the Reserve Bank was widely expected to deliver the fourth interest rate hike of 2026 at its board meeting next week in another attempt to tame inflation. The RBA hoped this year’s three interest rate rises would tame inflation – but nothing is going their way Read more While the consumer price index – Australia’s official inflation metric – increased by 0.6% in the March-to-June quarter, according to government data cited by Choice, the food categories all rose by more than the overall rate. Choice found about half of the overall increase came from strawberries, which became 37% more expensive on average over the three-month period – going from $4.68 to $6.41. There were also higher prices on average for mince, milk and avocados, while apples and basmati rice were cheaper, Choice said. Overall, the cost of the grocery basket increased the most at IGA, with prices up by 11% on average from $45.42 in March to $50.42 in June. Aldi had the second-biggest increase at 8% – with the total average cost of the items rising from $37.14 in March to $40.10 in June. However, Aldi’s basket remained the cheapest overall compared with IGA and the two major supermarkets. View image in fullscreen Choice found about half of the overall price increase came from strawberries. Photograph: Erik Anderson/AAP At Coles the average total price of the eight items was $42.54 in June, up by 6% or $2.44 since March, when the same basket was $$40.10. Woolworths recorded the smallest increase in price in the three-month period. At Australia’s largest supermarket chain, the basket went up by 2% or 0.87 cents – from $40.08 to $40.95. In addition to the base basket of items, Choice also surveyed what it called a “spotlight basket” of 10 items shoppers might buy on a health kick. In this basket were baby spinach, broccoli, carrots, chicken breast, corn thins, Greek-style yoghurt, hummus, tinned chickpeas and rolled oats. Choice found that Aldi again provided the best value, with the basket of healthy products costing $28.79. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Politics, really Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you after newsletter promotion At Woolworths, the basket cost $33.52, while the Coles basket came in at $34.25. IGA’s basket was the most expensive at $42.27. In order to work out the average cost for both baskets, Choice mystery shoppers priced groceries at 27 Woolworths, 27 Coles, 23 Aldi and 27 IGA stores. An Aldi spokesperson said Choice had “once again confirmed that [it] remains Australia’s best value supermarket”. Parenting advocate says family pressures are a 'policy failure' – video “We’re committed to making quality groceries more affordable and helping Australians stretch their budgets further,” they said. In short, we will not be beaten on the cost of the weekly shop.” A Coles spokesperson said the “vast majority” of its products either remained at the same price or became cheaper between March and June. “We’ll continue working hard to provide customers with great value, quality and convenience every time they shop with us,” they said. An IGA spokesperson said it was hard to comment on Choice’s findings in detail without the “full” methodology, but its stores were “more competitive than ever, with many stores matching or beating the major chains on key grocery lines”. Woolworths was contacted for comment. The Albanese government has funded Choice to carry out the quarterly surveys of grocery prices since 2024 as one of its cost-of-living measures, with two more reports due under the agreement. The final two surveys will be the first conducted after the implementation of new laws against “price gouging”, which came into effect on 1 July. https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/10/17/mag.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter hétfőn elmondja, mit terveznek a 2027-es költségvetéssel Gazdaság Bánáti Anna Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Jövő hét hétfőn napirend előtti felszólalásában a 2027-es költségvetést fogja bemutatni Magyar Péter, a miniszterelnök erről szombat délután posztolt a Facebookon. Magyar a költségvetést „az igazságosság és a fejlődés” költségvetésének hívta, ami szerinte az újjáépítésről fog szólni. (Az elmúlt 16 évben az Orbán-kormányok is többször nevezték el a költségvetéseiket , a 2025-öst békeköltségvetésnek címkézték fel, a 2026-os a háborúellenes költségvetés nevet kapta.) A kormányfő azt ígéri, a 2027-es költségvetésben spórolni fognak az állam működésén és a milliárdosoktól, valamint a szennyező cégektől csoportosítanak át „az eddig magára hagyott milliókhoz”. „Tesszük ezt úgy, hogy eközben az Orbánék által tönkretett költségvetést stabilizáljuk és az uniós ezermilliárdoknak köszönhetően soha nem látott mértékű beruházásokat indítunk el a lakhatás, a közlekedés és a vízügy területén.” A Fidesz-kormányok az elmúlt években a költségvetési törvényein többször is módosítottak menet közben , a célszámok menet közbeni igazításokkal folyamatosan változtak. A 2027-es költségvetéssel várhatóan nem ez lesz a helyzet, a mostani törvény már csak amiatt is kiemelt figyelmet kap, mert lesz az első olyan költségvetés, amit a Tisza-kormány már nem az előző kormánytól örökölt. A mostani kormány fontos célja a költségvetési hiány csökkentése , közben viszont célkitűzése az is, hogy ösztönözze a gazdasági növekedést, a beruházásokat és megőrizze az áprilisi választás után visszatérő befektetői bizalmat. A költségvetés alakításának mozgásterét az is befolyásolja, hogy Magyarország egyértelműen elköteleződne az euró bevezetése mellett .
